stories.headline: Hyderabad jolted by mysterious boom and tremors, experts rule out major earthquake
stories.title: Hyderabad jolted by mysterious boom and tremors, experts rule out major earthquake
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A mysterious boom and brief ground vibrations sent residents rushing outdoors across several Hyderabad neighbourhoods, prompting scientists to explain the possible geological cause.

A deafening boom, trembling floors and terrified residents rushing out of their homes turned an otherwise ordinary Tuesday morning into a scene of panic across Hyderabad's south-western outskirts, after an unexplained burst of sound and ground vibrations rattled several residential neighbourhoods.
Residents across Rajendranagar, Upparpally, Attapur, Erraboda, Keshavswamy Nagar and Langar Houz reported the incident at around 10.25 am on October 27.
The vibrations reportedly lasted five to 10 seconds, rattling windows and shifting household utensils, leaving many people wondering whether an earthquake had struck the city.
As alarm spread across the affected localities, residents stepped out of their homes and gathered in open spaces, fearing that the tremors could signal a larger seismic event.
The sudden, explosion-like noise added to the confusion, prompting speculation about its origin.

However, scientists at the Hyderabad-based National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) moved to dispel reports of a major tectonic earthquake, pointing instead to a localised geological process known as hydro seismicity as a possible explanation for the phenomenon.
What caused the mysterious boom?
Experts say that Hyderabad's geological setting offers important clues to understanding the incident.
The city lies on a stable crystalline granite shield, making a destructive earthquake highly unlikely.
Nevertheless, localised micro-seismic activity can occur beneath the surface.
Water penetrating deep into the ground, particularly amid intense seasonal or persistent rainfall, can enter tiny pores and fractures in underground rock formations.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: South Coast Railway cancels 53 trains, sets up 24/7 war room
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: South Coast Railway cancels 53 trains, sets up 24/7 war room
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The South Coast Railway Zone has cancelled 53 trains and established a 24-hour war room as part of its preparations for the approaching very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, with heavy rainfall and strong winds expected to affect railway operations.
Sandeep Mathur, General Manager of the South Coast Railway Zone, reviewed disaster management preparations and precautionary measures to protect passengers, railway staff and train services.
He held a meeting with four Divisional Railway Managers (DRMs) and other officials to assess the zone's readiness.

According to an official press release issued on Monday, war rooms have been set up at the zonal headquarters and divisional headquarters to improve coordination and enable a prompt response to emergencies.
The 53 cancelled trains were scheduled to run between various origin and destination points across the north Andhra region and Guntur.
The railway zone has also stepped up surveillance of vulnerable bridges, railway tracks, yards and signalling systems.
Officials are clearing silt, vegetation and debris from catch-water drains and drainage channels to reduce the risk of waterlogging during heavy rainfall.
Patrol personnel and watchmen have been deployed at vulnerable locations, while emergency track maintenance materials have been stocked to support rapid repairs if required.
Mathur has directed railway officials to coordinate closely with state government authorities and keep monitoring weather advisories issued by the meteorological department.
The South Coast Railway Zone has strengthened passenger assistance arrangements ahead of the storm.
Help desks are being established at major stations to provide timely updates, while additional counters will be operated to facilitate refunds for cancelled tickets, where applicable.
Catering units have been instructed to maintain adequate food supplies.

stories.headline: Minister Tummala Nageshwara Rao cautions officials and people over cyclone Arnab
stories.title: Minister Tummala Nageshwara Rao cautions officials and people over cyclone Arnab
stories.summary: Telangana Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao urges officials and farmers in Khammam district to take precautions against Cyclone Arnab, protect crops, conserve irrigation water and ensure uninterrupted drinking water and power supply.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Telangana Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao urges officials and farmers in Khammam district to take precautions against Cyclone Arnab, protect crops, conserve irrigation water and ensure uninterrupted drinking water and power supply.
Agriculture and Marketing Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao asked officials to take precautions to tackle drinking water and irrigation supply issues in undivided Khammam district.
During a review meeting at Khammam Collectorate, he discussed ways to protect crops after cyclone, Irrigation water, drinking water and Electricity supply.
He urged officials of the Irrigation Department to create awareness in villages and ask farmers to grow other crops instead of paddy during upcoming Yasangi (rabi) season.
He also advised them to conserve water used from Seetharama Project canals and Nagarjuna Sagar Left Canal.
The official were asked to take suitable steps to close canal shutters.
Farmers were requested to protect their standing crops from the cyclone Arnab.
They were asked to constantly monitor the situation along with officials from the Department of Agriculture, Horticulture and Marketing.
Marketing officials should also help farmers get good market rates for crops and pre-plan to ensure smooth procurement.
Departments were requested to work together to ensure there are no shortages of drinking water and power due to El Niño.
There should be no negligence from officials regarding supply of drinking water to the public or essential services to farmers.
Preventative action should also be taken to avoid losses due to lack of irrigation water.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Bapatla district issues emergency helpline numbers
stories.summary: The district administration has established a 24-hour control room to respond to emergencies
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bapatla district Collector Dr. V. Vinod Kumar has issued emergency helpline numbers to help people seek assistance during cyclonic conditions, heavy rain and other emergency situations.
According to a statement issued on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the district administration has established a 24-hour control room to respond to emergencies.
The public can contact the District Control Room at 08643-220226.
People can also reach the WhatsApp helpline at 8712417880 and share their geographical location to facilitate assistance.
For power supply-related emergencies, the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (APCPDCL) has provided separate contact numbers for different areas.
The Bapatla Circle helpline is 92814 13774, while the numbers for the Bapatla and Repalle divisions are 94910 52945 and 94408 17597.
The administration has also announced helpline numbers for Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) offices.
The Repalle RDO office can be contacted at 08648-293795 or 94407 80426.
The Chirala RDO office number is 87126 55910, while the Bapatla RDO office can be reached at 94938 03524.
The district administration has urged people to use these helplines to report emergencies and seek assistance during adverse weather conditions.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: Flash floods alert issued in parts of AP
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Flash floods alert issued in parts of AP
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh issues a red alert as Cyclone Arnab intensifies over the Bay of Bengal, bringing warnings of heavy rainfall, 100 kmph winds, flash floods and school closures across coastal districts.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh issues a red alert as Cyclone Arnab intensifies over the Bay of Bengal, bringing warnings of heavy rainfall, 100 kmph winds, flash floods and school closures across coastal districts.
The meteorological department has issued a red alert in Andhra Pradesh due to Cyclone Arnab, which has intensified into very severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal.
The department is forecasting rains in most part of the state with possibility of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, especially in the coastal districts.
Gale force winds are likely along the coast with speed of 90-100kmph.
A APSDMA MD Prakhar Jain asked people to stay alert, especially the people residing in hilly and low-lying areas.

There is an issuance of flash floods warning in 14 districts, namely Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Kakinada, East Godavari, Yanam, Konaseema, West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, NTR and Alluri Sitharama Raju.
Two days holidays have been announced in coastal and North Andhra districts.
These districts include Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Manyam, Alluri, Kakinada, Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Polavaram, Eluru, Krishna, NTR and Guntur.
In Anakapalli district schools would be closed from the 27th, 28th and 29th.
In other news, the meteorological department has also forecast rains in Telangana with possibilities of thunderstorms, lightning and gusty wind in some areas.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab intensifies: Kolkata may see rain later this week
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab intensifies: Kolkata may see rain later this week
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab is heading towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, but its indirect impact could bring rain to Kolkata and several districts of West Bengal this week.
Kolkata may see a change in weather this week as Cyclone Arnab intensifies over the Bay of Bengal and moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.

Although the storm is not expected to make landfall in West Bengal, its indirect impact could bring rainfall to the city and several other districts, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The cyclone intensified from a deep depression to a cyclonic storm early Monday and later strengthened into a severe cyclonic storm.
It is expected to intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday morning, October 27, as it continues moving towards the eastern coast.
The IMD has forecast rainfall in Kolkata and other parts of Gangetic West Bengal on October 28 and 29.
While some areas could see heavy showers, rainfall intensity and distribution will depend on the cyclone's movement and prevailing weather conditions.
Kolkata remained largely sunny on Monday.
Tuesday's forecast suggests light rain or thundershowers, with generally cloudy skies expected by the afternoon.
Persistent cloud cover and rainfall could affect daytime temperatures, while increased atmospheric moisture may keep night temperatures relatively high.
Which parts of Bengal could receive rain?
Southern districts of West Bengal are likely to experience rainfall from Tuesday, with a more significant spell expected between Wednesday and Saturday.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: DIBRUGARH: The Rotary Club of Dibrugarh has reached out to 380 beneficiaries across four villages in Charaideo and Sivasagar districts under the first phase of its Winter Relief Distribution Programme, aimed at supporting families severely affected by floods in Upper Assam.
The relief materials were distributed in Chuladhara Sokial Gaon, Moran Gaon, and Borgaon in Charaideo district, and Duarah Gaon in Sivasagar district.

Essential items, including blankets, mosquito nets, bedsheets, sanitary pads, bags, and other necessities, were provided to help vulnerable families meet their basic needs and prepare for the winter season.

The relief initiative received generous support from the Rotary Club of Delhi Southend Next under Rotary International District 3011, highlighting the spirit of inter-club cooperation and humanitarian service.

stories.headline: UP Election Body Apologises Over ‘Ram Didn’t Kill Any Minority’ Remark After Voter Slip Error
stories.title: UP Election Body Apologises Over ‘Ram Didn’t Kill Any Minority’ Remark After Voter Slip Error
stories.summary: Meta Description: Uttar Pradesh's election body apologised for the tone and language of a controversial remark after a voter list error involving the name Ramhit Yadav triggered caste bias allegations from AAP MP Sanjay Singh.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Meta Description: Uttar Pradesh's election body apologised for the tone and language of a controversial remark after a voter list error involving the name Ramhit Yadav triggered caste bias allegations from AAP MP Sanjay Singh.
The Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer’s office on Tuesday apologised for the tone and language of a controversial comment made in response to an error in a voter list.
The controversy began after an incorrect entry involving the name ‘Ramhit Yadav’ triggered criticism from Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MP Sanjay Singh.
The controversy came in the wake of ‘Ramhit Yadav' being allegedly included in the voter list for the recent Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council polls under the name ‘Ram ne Yadav ko Maara'.
Reacting to the mistake, Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on social media, asking why the error appeared to target a particular caste.
In a post on X, the AAP leader asked whether the computer system was casteist and accused the Election Commission of potentially pursuing the agenda of a political party.
He also questioned why similar errors had not appeared against surnames such as Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai and Bisht.

Responding to Singh’s allegations, the office of Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa pointed to another instance in which a voter’s father’s name was allegedly recorded incorrectly as ‘Ram ne Sharma ko Maara’ (Ram hit Sharma).
The office cited the second example to argue that the mistakes were errors in the voter list rather than evidence of caste-based discrimination.
However, the poll body later apologised for the tone and language used in its response, amid growing criticism over the remark.
The row has emerged at a time when the Election Commission is facing protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
The controversy has added to the scrutiny surrounding the poll body and its handling of voter-list-related issues.

stories.headline: Can Election Expenses Be Recovered From Candidate Who Resigns To Re-Contest For Another Party? Supreme Court To Decide
stories.title: Can Election Expenses Be Recovered From Candidate Who Resigns To Re-Contest For Another Party? Supreme Court To Decide
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today issued notice on a plea raising the issue of election expenditure recovery from a candidate who resigns after getting elected from one political party in order to recontest from another party.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order, calling for the response of the Union, the Election Commission of India, the Chief Electoral Officer, Tamil Nadu, certain MLAs in Tamil Nadu who resigned from their posts and sought to re-contest in bye-elections, and others.

The petitioner, a practicing advocate, challenges a Madras High Court order, which dismissed his writ petition seeking a writ of mandamus to ECI and CEO, Tamil Nadu to frame an "Election Expenditure Security" mechanism as well as a 5-year disqualification from Parliamentary/State Assembly elections for voluntarily resigning legislators (without compelling reason).

The writ petition before the High Court claimed that after the 2026 Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, 6 elected members (AIADMK) resigned from their seats within a short span of results being declared.
These members were - S Jayakumar, Maragatham Kumaravel, P Sathyabama, Dr Esakki Subbaya, C Vijaya Bhaskar, and MR VIjayabhaskar.
It was claimed that the resignations were voluntary, without any compelling circumstance, and necessitated bye-elections in the respective constituencies (to be funded by the public exchequer).
The petitioner urged that the public ought not be made to pay twice for the same seat because of an individual's personal or political choice to give it up.

The "Election Expenditure Security" mechanism proposed by the petitioner called for a pre-deposit by an MLA who resigned and wished to re-contest in the bye-election occasioned by their resignation (deposit amount being equal to the amount spent on the bye-election).
The High Court observed that it could not convert an executive or legislative option into a judicial command.
(ii) whether the public trust doctrine extends to the electoral mandate conferred by the people and to the public funds expended in securing it?
While filing the petition, the petitioner also sought certain interim reliefs.
He prayed for stay of all further proceedings in the bye-elections to Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies, including the poll scheduled on October 6.

stories.title: Tata Motors secures Iveco takeover as 87.81% shareholders back €3.91-billion deal
stories.summary: Acquisition to give Indian manufacturer larger presence across Europe, Latin America
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tata Motors has secured the decisive shareholder backing for its €3.91-billion takeover of Italian truckmaker Iveco after investors representing 87.81% of its equity accepted the offer on Monday, overcoming minority shareholder resistance and clearing the biggest hurdle in its 15-month pursuit.
The acquisition sets the stage for a global commercial-vehicle group with combined annual revenue of approximately €21 billion and sales exceeding 590,000 vehicles.
A Teleborsa update published on Borsa Italiana’s website on October 26 confirmed that 238,157,212 shares had been tendered.

“Complessivamente le richieste di adesione raggiungono quota 238.157.212, pari al 87,81% circa,” it stated, meaning total acceptances had reached 238,157,212 shares, equivalent to approximately 87.81%.
The acceptance comfortably exceeded the revised 80% threshold, paving the way for settlement and integration of the two businesses.
First announced in July 2025, the transaction carries an estimated enterprise value of $4.5 billion.
Tata Motors Managing Director and CEO Girish Wagh had anticipated the late surge.

“As is typically seen in tender offer processes, a significant proportion of shares tend to be tendered towards the very end of the acceptance period, particularly in the final 24 to 48 hours,” he told investors on Friday.
Shareholder acceptance jumped from approximately 52% on October 23 to 87.81% on October 26, reflecting a sharp increase in participation towards the deadline.
Exor, the Agnelli family’s investment company and Iveco’s largest shareholder, had already committed its 27.06% holding.
However, activist investor Petrus Advisers challenged the valuation, arguing that Tata’s offer undervalued Iveco.
Tata raised its offer from €14.10 to €14.40 per share on October 9, an increase of 2.1%, describing the revised consideration as its best and final price.

article_sentences: The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which has members drawn from across the media spectrum, including those owned by the Ambani and Adani Groups, have challenged the Union government’s privacy law as a violation of journalistic freedom.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear a batch of petitions filed by activists on October 27.

The petition filed by the DNPA, which is also listed before the Bench, challenged specific provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025.
The DNPA said the law was completely in contravention with the law laid down by the Supreme Court in its privacy judgment, which held the right inviolable and fundamental to human dignity and life.
“They impermissibly restrict the fundamental right to information and freedom of speech and expression,” the petition said.

The law fails “to provide any exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class of processing, entitled to constitutional protection under Article 14 and 19(l)(a) of the Constitution of India and threatens the full spectrum of Journalistic activity carried out by journalists, ground reporters, citizens, whistleblowers, RTI activists, and other stakeholders, and strikes at the core of our democratic framework and runs contrary to the basic tenets of the Constitution of India,” the petition said.
It said publishers, editors, reporters and correspondents were, as a consequence of the law, brought within a regime of notice and prior consent, compelled erasure, and verifiable consent.

Section 36 of the DPDP Act, read with Rule 23 and the Seventh Schedule of the DPDP Rules, vested the Central government with an unbridled and standardless authority to requisition any information from any data fiduciary or intermediary, unaccompanied by judicial oversight, any requirement of necessity or proportionality, or notice to the affected data principal.
“Such a power is capable of being turned to the identification and targeting of journalistic sources and is thus constitutionally infirm,” the petition said.
Section 44 (3) of the DPDP Act, by amending Section 8 (1 )(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, has placed every category of “personal information” beyond the reach of disclosure.
Further, by amending the Right to Information Act 2005, the DPDP Act has created an absolute bar on the seeking of information relating to public offices.

article_sentences: The 3-month pregnant journalist who was allegedly pushed by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi during the gathering in the Supreme Court on October 12, when Gandhi came to file the INDIA bloc's writ petition against SIR, has moved the Supreme Court seeking impleadment in a case related to political demonstrations within Court premises.
The applicant alleges that Gandhi pushed her during the Opposition leaders' march to the Supreme Court on October 12, at which time she was 11 weeks and 3 days pregnant.
“Respondent No.4 suddenly pushed her towards the gate, with such force that she lost her balance and fell, and had to break the fall with her hands.

The push was delivered openly, in a crowded place, in the presence of security personnel, journalists and other persons, despite her express pleas, and was not a mere jostle of the crowd”, the application states.
Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia orally mentioned the application before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant today, following which the bench ordered notice to the respondents.
It is alleged that in the fall, the applicant's phone was shattered and the receiver of the microphone clipped to her collar was dislodged.
The incident was recorded by the applicant's cameraperson, and her voice can be heard on the recording made by her microphone.
The applicant avers that after the fall, she developed pain in the lower abdomen and was taken to the Casualty ward of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital at around 9 pm.
From there, she was discharged with medication, advice for further scans and screening, and instructions to report immediately in case of pain, bleeding or leaking.

“The fall, the fear for her unborn child, and the humiliation of being pushed to the ground in public at the gate of the highest court of the land have caused the Applicant grave physical and mental trauma.”
The applicant contends that she repeatedly pleaded “Sir, I am being pushed” and “Please don't push, sir” but her “pleas were drowned out by the workers” of Congress chanting “Rahul Gandhi Zindabad”.
The plea claims that even after she was pushed, no one stopped to help her.
